process_smoke.scope: Local TCP/WebSocket, signed Google fixtures, real process shutdown and restart; not live Google or Railway
checks_detail: All shipped web files and icons served byte-for-byte
Save files and server source are not served over HTTP
Legacy username/password registration cannot bypass mandatory Google
Create and enter as wizard using Google-authenticated WebSocket
Two separate clients share the same world
Server executes an actual first-circle spell
Arcane Recovery completes short rest, restores mana and consumes its long-rest resource
Hotbar update round-trips through the real game server
SIGTERM closes connected clients and exits cleanly within draining budget
Last hotbar change, actual spell history and used Recovery persist on shutdown
Restart snapshots the existing save before opening the game
Same account logs in after process restart with its saved settings
Used Arcane Recovery remains spent after the real process restart

fixture_updates_and_limits: Historical smoke expected Bractwo 0.8.17, anonymous password login and immediate Arcane Recovery with a 180-second cooldown. UI22 health/auth expectations were updated; the stale Recovery fixture now verifies the existing short-rest completion and persistent long-rest resource. No gameplay production code was changed.
The UI20 continent cold import exceeded the historical ten-second readiness budget; only startup readiness was raised to thirty seconds. Shutdown still must complete in fifteen seconds.

The old smoke requested full snapshots and left its second client unread, delaying state observations. The final fixture uses the actual browser owner-delta protocol and consumes both clients. Full gameplay, save and restart assertions pass.

The subprocess uses the real Google token verifier with locally RSA-signed fixtures and a test-only public-key certificate transport. Production run.py has no fixture login or certificate override. No real Google account, deployed Railway service or credentials were used.
Suite totals are reported individually; tests/test_google_security_ui22.py may also appear in the main Python QA report and should not be double-counted.
